key_insight: Q-DICE makes distributed quantum computing practical to study on classical simulators and NISQ hardware by compiling circuits with hardware-aware boundary constraints and realistic interconnect noise.
engineering_relevance: It gives researchers a way to benchmark and co-design distributed quantum systems before physical large-scale hardware is available.
method: Builds distributed QPU backends using QPU slicing and stitching.
Models nonlocal link noise with Kraus operators and stochastic error channels.
Uses a boundary-aware transpiler to enforce distributed topology constraints.
evidence_signal: The authors validate Q-DICE on multiple experimentally demonstrated circuits, including distributed Grover's search, and report a worst-case fidelity deviation of 4% versus experiments.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on how well the assumed noise models and topology constraints match a target hardware stack.
paper_title: Q-DICE: Quantum Distributed Interconnect Compiler and Emulator
